CARUS Imperator Probi exercitum bello latè victorem in Persida ducens, hostile regnum vastavit: Seleuciam cinctam Euphrate, quam olim ceperat Ælius VERUS Antoninus, expugnavit: Ctesiphontem deinde petentem, & longius progredi volentem, ictus fulminis cœlo turbido & coruscante absumsit. Sic & 284.JULIANUS Apostata, Alexandrum Magnum in mo-narchiâ Persarum occupandâ æmulari cupiens, Euphratem cum exercitu transgressus, justissimas suæ impietatis & tyrannidis pœnas persolvit. Sic nec versus Septentrionem ultra Mithridatis regnum in Ponto ascenderunt Romani. SESOSTRIS Rex Ægypti potentissimus, orbis Imperium affectans, postquam totam Asiam victricibus armis penetravit, in Colchide tandem victus est: teste Diodoro lib.1.c.4. In eadem vi-363.cinia à Tomyri Massagetarum Regina victus & occisus est CYRUS Medus: teste Herodoto lib.1. DARIUS 458.quoque Hystaspis, Persarum Rex, contra Scythas profectus, re infecta domum rediit. Herod. lib.4. ALEXANDER verò Magnus, feris Septentrionis gentibus non irritatis, portas Caspias, ferratis repagulis obseratas, claudit: ut gentes Scythicas hoc modo ab Asiæ adi-465.tu arceret: ut in ejus vitâ scribit Plutarchus. Sic & TURCÆ in omnibus fere bellis cum Persis infelicissimi, maximis acceptis cladibus, intra fatales limites subinde revocati sunt.
main_text.head: FLOS XIIX.
Fatales omnium regnorum & imperiorum sunt periodi.

page.notes: Section numbers in the left margin read "283.", "284.", "363.", "458." and "465."; the third and fourth are slightly unclear in the scan (possibly "3458" and "3465" as printed). The heading number reads "XIIX" as printed, possibly a misprint for XIX; caput value taken as 19 with that doubt. Printed signs in the margin are section marks, not notes of content. Running head and page number are clear. The catchword "gente-" is the start of the next line, which is at the foot of the page.
